title: What the numbers can and cannot say about soil carbon
intro: A guided tour of one dataset: what is measured, what is modelled, and where the uncertainty actually lives.

add_content_to_page.add_paragraph: The dataset behind this story covers 36 plots, two depths and four annual campaigns. Before any conclusion, it is worth separating three different things the numbers can mean: a measurement, an estimate and a projection.

add_focus_list.heading: The headline figures
items_of_the_focus_list: Reported uncertainty: standard deviation across cores.

add_image.image_alt: A chart-like arrangement of soil samples
add_image.image_caption: Cores arranged by depth before analysis.

add_content_to_page.add_paragraph: The measurement is the mass of carbon in a known volume of soil. The estimate is the plot mean, with its spread. The projection — how much carbon a catchment might hold under a different management — is a model, and models inherit every assumption in the sampling design.

add_special_note.heading: The part not in the data
add_special_note.text: Winter stocks were not sampled. Any annual figure therefore describes the spring condition, not the year. The archive says so in the README, and so should every chart drawn from it.
